subject: MAP: Throughput benchmarking results + unit-econ summary / close cadence
messages:
From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@meridian-pay.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Sokolova <elena.s@meridian-pay.com>, payments-team@meridian-pay.com
Date: 2026-06-05T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff / throughput targets

Neha —

Thanks for the MAP draft. Quick context from our side: primary production workload is a payments reconciliation assistant (multi-turn, avg 220 tokens/request, 90% calls are < 512 tokens). Target is to serve 400 sustained QPS during peak windows with TTFT < 120ms and 99th perc latency under 450ms.

Before we sign the MAP, can Redwood show throughput results for a realistic traffic mix (20% chat, 80% single-turn generation) and provide a unit-econ snapshot (cost per 1M tokens and cost per sustained QPS)? We need that baked into the MAP to justify the commit.

Tom
Head of Platform
Meridian Payments
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@meridian-pay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-05T12:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff / throughput targets

Tom —

Appreciate the clarity. We've updated the MAP to include a focused benchmarking plan and a milestone-backed decision path. High level: 
- Test environment: Redwood Dedicated (p3-dedicated pool) configured with 8xA100-equivalents, model variant: open-llama-70b-8bit (quantized), optimized kernel set.
- Traffic mix: 80% single-turn generation (avg 220 tokens), 20% multi-turn (avg 5 turns, avg 180 tokens/turn).
- Metrics captured: sustained QPS, tokens/sec, TTFT, per-request latency percentiles (50/95/99), memory/KV cache hit rate, and cost units.
- Run cadence: two sustained 30-minute ramps + one 3-hour soak at target concurrency.
- Deliverables: throughput CSV, TTFT traces, unit-econ sheet, and MAP updated with go/no-go decision gates.

We'll kick off the first run tomorrow morning PST. Attaching MAP_v1.3.pdf for your review.

Next steps: If the results match the MAP thresholds (TTFT < 120ms, sustained QPS >= 400 at 95% success) — we iterate on pricing and finalize the commitment line in week of 6/14.

Attached: MAP_v1.3.pdf

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_v1.3.pdf (PDF, 0.9MB)]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-06T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: benchmarking knobs and billing assumptions

Internal quick notes before the run — copying into thread after validation.
- Kernel/CPU pinning: ensure kernel set A is used (we saw 8% perf delta vs B on short sequences).
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for 80% flow to reduce tokens/sec by ~12%.
- Batching policy: 6-8 dynamic batch size for 220-token avg; set latency SLO at 200ms for batch flush fallback.
- Billing model used for unit econ: hosted-equivalent pricing converted to customer committed nodes (we amortize infra + support + margin). Base assumptions listed in unit_econ_summary_20260607.xlsx (attached).

I'll run the scripted workload at 13:00 PST today. Neha — share the public CSV and I'll sanity-check.

— Rishi
Director, Product — Performance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: run_script_v2.sh (text, 8KB)]
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@meridian-pay.com>, Elena Sokolova <elena.s@meridian-pay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-06T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Benchmark results (summary) + unit econ highlights

Tom / Elena —

We completed the runs this afternoon. Summary (see attached CSV + unit econ workbook):

Key throughput & latency:
- Sustained target: 400 QPS goal (mixed traffic) — achieved 410 QPS sustained over 3 hours (95% CI +/- 3 QPS).
- Tokens/sec (aggregate): 78,500 tokens/sec sustained at peak soak.
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): median 85ms, 95th 160ms, 99th 320ms.
- End-to-end latency (generation complete): median 240ms, 95th 420ms, 99th 610ms (99th spike correlated with occasional GC on host — we recommend enabling soft-affinity).
- Concurrency: test used 600 concurrent connections to hit 410 sustained QPS given the mix.
- KV cache hit rate: 72% for multi-turn flows (reduced tokens/sec by ~10% vs cold).

Unit economics (high level):
- Total infra cost (amortized) to serve 1M tokens: $12.40
- Effective cost per sustained QPS (24/7 amortized on committed nodes + support): $18.10 / sustained QPS / month
- Customer-facing proposal (with discount tiers in MAP): $14.00 / 1M tokens; committed node pricing equivalent to $13.00 / sustained QPS (monthly)
- Break-even token volume to justify dedicated pool vs hosted: ~45M tokens / month

Attachments: throughput_results_20260606.csv, unit_econ_summary_20260607.xlsx (sheet 'customer_view' contains the pricing ladder and sensitivity).

Action items proposed in MAP update:
1) PO + signatures for a 6-month reserved pool by 6/18 to lock committed-node price.
2) One-week production pilot (copy of test config) to be scheduled 6/21–6/28.
3) Post-pilot: finalize SLA addendum and run an on-site architecture review (if desired).

Tom — does this align with your procurement windows? If yes, we'll add the PO milestone to the MAP and circulate for signatures.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: throughput_results_20260606.csv (CSV, 2.1MB)]
From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@meridian-pay.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Sokolova <elena.s@meridian-pay.com>, payments-team@meridian-pay.com, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-07T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark results (summary) + unit econ highlights

Neha / team —

This looks solid and answers the key questions. A couple quick clarifications before we finalize the MAP: 
- The 99th gen-complete latency at 610ms is above our internal guardrail of 500ms. Is the GC spike something you can mitigate for production or a sign we need a higher-spec pool?
- We prefer the committed-node pricing if the 6-month PO is signed by 6/18. Procurement will circulate a PO draft by EOD 6/11.

Assuming we get the PO in that window and the pilot goes well (6/21–6/28), we can close the deal by 7/02. Please add a canary fallback policy in the MAP to traffic-shift if 99th breaches 500ms in the pilot.

I'll sign off on the MAP_v1.3 once we get the PO draft.

Tom Harris
Head of Platform — Meridian Payments
[Attachment: PO_template_draft.docx (DOCX, 45KB)]
